2025_141_1_21_aarc_boe_presentation_fina.paragraph: Presented to the Troy School District Board of Education on January 21, 2025, this Attendance Area Review Committee (AARC) proposal deck narrows the middle school boundary discussion to variations of Option C after the January 14, 2025 Board workshop. Under the full Option C, projected Fall 2027 middle school enrollments would be Baker 616, Boulan Park 603, Larson 625 and Smith 682, affecting 5 schools, moving approximately 630 students and meeting all three stated goals. The deck also newly quantifies the Troy Union Elementary and Somerset Apartments populations that drive the alternatives, and lays out community listening sessions and a survey before any Board decision in April or May.

**Item.** Attendance Area Review Committee (AARC) proposal presentation to the Troy School District Board of Education, January 21, 2025. It revises the January 14 deck by replacing Options A through E with Option C and three Option C variants developed after the 1/14/25 Board workshop.

**Background.** Prior AARC groups convened in 2015 and 2018, and a 62-member Facilities Review Committee ran a 6-month process in 2021/22 producing recommendations for the 2022 bond proposal. Middle school enrollment ranges from 590 to 870 per building. Plante Moran was hired as demographers. The 2024 AARC had 25 members (15 administrators, 10 community members) and met October 14, October 28, November 11, November 25 and December 9; cabinet discussions have been weekly since August 2024.

**Optimal size model.** Learning Community size of 125 students; average class size 25; full-time teachers teach 5 sections (5x25 = 125); two learning communities per grade level (250 in grade 6); grades 6-8 totaling 750 students, flexing up to 900. The new Smith Middle School was built for an optimal enrollment of 750, and all four middle schools rank in Metro Parent's Top 6 in Michigan.

**Goals.** Goal 1 - right-size middle schools with equal student ratios. Goal 2 - resolve double splits. Goal 3 - no impact on high schools.

**Baseline enrollment.**

| Middle school | Existing boundary (Dec 2024) | Maintain existing boundary (2027) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baker (Blue) | 631 | 556 |
| Boulan (Orange) | 847 | 721 |
| Larson (Green) | 863 | 713 |
| Smith (Yellow) | 599 | 536 |

Four middle schools total 2,940 pupils (2024) and a projected 2,526 pupils (2027).

**Options presented.**

| Option | Baker | Boulan Park | Larson | Smith | Schools affected | Students moved | Goals met |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Option C | 616 | 603 | 625 | 682 | 5 | ~630 | 3 |
| Option C - ONLY TU | 517 | 793 | 625 | 591 | 3 | ~250 | 2 |
| Option C - ONLY SA | 616 | 603 | 750 | 557 | 3 | ~380 | 2 |
| Option C - TU to Larson | 616 | 603 | 830 | 477 | 6 | ~380 | 2 |
| No Change | 517 | 793 | 750 | 466 | 0 | n/a | 1 |

**Driver populations.** Troy Union Elementary is projected at 205 students for Fall 2027: 100 assigned to Smith, 105 assigned to Larson, with 20 open-enrolled from Smith to Larson, yielding actual counts of 80 to Smith and 125 to Larson. Somerset Apartments is projected at 319 elementary students for Fall 2027, all of whom attend Boulan Park Middle School under current policy.

**Impacts.** Each option notes potential special education staffing effects, continued building-by-building staffing for special education and English learners, and transportation in which routes and bus numbers may shift while keeping driver numbers consistent and the longest route at 30 minutes or less.

**Timeline and next steps.** 2025/2026 prepare for adjustments; 2026/2027 changes implemented. Students in grades 5-8 (classes of 2032, 2031, 2030, 2029) are not impacted and may continue in their Fall 2025 building; current 5th and 6th graders slotted for a new school may move in 2025/2026. Community meetings at the four middle schools in February/March, a community survey in March/April, and Board consideration and decision in April/May.
2025_141_1_21_aarc_boe_presentation_fina.verbose:
**Document and setting.** Attendance Area Review Committee (AARC) Proposal presentation, Troy School District, delivered to the Board of Education on January 21, 2025. It is a revision of the AARC deck given at the January 14, 2025 Board workshop: the earlier Options A through E are removed and replaced with Option C plus three Option C variants built in response to Board and committee questions.

**Why the review.** Historic district practice is to review enrollment patterns and challenges every 5-10 years. Previous AARC groups convened in 2015 and 2018, and a 62-member Facilities Review Committee ran a 6-month process in 2021/22 to create recommendations for the 2022 bond proposal with staff, student, cabinet and Board of Education feedback. Challenges include enrollment 'splits' as students transition from elementary to middle school or middle to high school, a double split at Troy Union, single splits at Smith, Baker, Wattles and Hamilton, and current ratios at each middle school, where enrollment ranges from 590 to 870 per building. Additional factors listed are enrollment projections, birth rate and schools of choice, the new Smith Middle School built for an optimal enrollment of 750, and Metro Parent rankings placing all four middle schools in the Top 6 in Michigan.

**Optimal middle school size.** Ideal parameters are a Learning Community size of 125 students, an average class size of 25 students, full-time teachers teaching 5 sections (5 x 25 = 125), two Learning Communities per grade level (250 in grade 6), and grades 6-8 totaling 750 students. Learning Communities can flex up to 900 students as class size increases above an average of 25, and to fewer than 750 students as class size dips below 25, which increases costs. Cited benefits include more full-time elective staff and 3 lunch periods aligned with grade levels.

A smaller school risks more partial staff, impact on school culture, limited course availability (example: only 2 sections of art offered), increased costs from lower class sizes, staff split across two content areas, and too few students for extracurriculars such as jazz band, theatre and yearbook. A larger school may require staffing 'overages' (example: more than a 1.0 orchestra teacher), teachers giving up prep periods, congestion in classrooms, hallways and cafeteria, saturated club and athletic opportunities, and limited ability to support new or move-in families.

**Process to date.** The district hired Plante Moran as demographers for yearly and future enrollment projections. The AARC group was formed in 2024 with 25 members representing each elementary and middle school - 15 administrators and 10 community members - drawn from applications requested in September. The 3-month process met on October 14, October 28, November 11, November 25 and December 9, and cabinet discussions have occurred weekly since August 2024. Criteria and data used included enrollment, grade cohorts and boundaries, birth rates, resident/non-resident/employee feeder paths, current maps, demographic data (ethnicity, English learners, students with disabilities, economics, content area performance), transportation implications, historical cohort data, and previous AARC information. Historical enrollment data slides are labeled January 2024. TSD directed the committee to focus on a four middle school future; committee feedback gave the district pause regarding community priorities and values such as programmatic experience, location and community schools, enrollment size, and duration of bus ride.

**Surrounding districts.** Rochester Community School District, Utica Community Schools, Walled Lake Consolidated Schools, Huron Valley Schools, West Bloomfield School District and Chippewa Valley Schools are described as considering or moving through the same process.

**Goals.** Goal 1: right-size middle schools, equal student ratios. Goal 2: resolve double splits. Goal 3: no impact on high schools.

**Current pathways.** Troy Union to Smith/Larson to Athens/Troy; Wass, Hill and Costello to Larson to Athens; Barnard to Baker to Athens; Morse and Wattles to Baker to Athens/Troy; Martell and Leonard to Smith to Troy; Hamilton to Smith/Boulan to Troy; Schroeder and Bemis to Boulan to Troy. The double split is Troy Union Elementary students splitting between Smith and Larson middle schools, with Smith students splitting again between Athens and Troy High. The elementary single split is Wattles and Morse students attending Baker MS splitting between Troy HS and Athens HS. The middle school single split is Hamilton students splitting between Smith and Boulan Park MS, with both feeding Troy HS.

**Current and future student counts.** All prior options presented assumed Somerset Apartment students would follow the feeder pattern. Four middle schools hold 2,940 pupils (2024) and a projected 2,526 pupils (2027). Existing Boundary (December 2024): Baker (Blue) 631 students, Boulan (Orange) 847 students, Larson (Green) 863 students, Smith (Yellow) 599 students. Maintain Existing Boundary (2027): Baker (Blue) 556, Boulan (Orange) 721, Larson (Green) 713, Smith (Yellow) 536.

**Fall 2027 projected middle school feeder enrollment (2,526 students).** Hamilton 226, Schroeder 216, Bemis 237, Martell 189, Leonard 212, Wattles 205, Morse 204, Troy Union 205, Costello 219, Wass 219, Hill 187, Barnard 207. All options are based on the Fall 2027 projected enrollment.

**Troy Union Elementary detail.** Fall 2027 projection of 205 students. Middle school students from Troy Union: 205. Troy Union assigned to Smith: 100. Troy Union assigned to Larson: 105. Troy Union open enrolled from Smith to Larson: 20. Actual students Troy Union to Smith: 80. Actual students Troy Union to Larson: 125.

**Somerset Apartments detail.** Fall 2027 elementary projection of 319 students, distributed as Hamilton 0, Schroeder 60, Bemis 69, Martell 39, Leonard 52, Wattles 52, Morse 47, Troy Union 0, Costello 0, Wass 0, Hill 0, Barnard 0. All Somerset Apartments students go to Boulan Park Middle School.

**Option C.** Baker 616, Boulan Park 603, Larson 625, Smith 682. Updated after the AARC concluded, based on questions asked by the group. All Troy Union students go to Smith. All students living in community housing follow their currently assigned elementary school to that elementary school's assigned middle school. Somerset Apartments' 319 students go to Boulan Park from 6 elementary schools. Number of schools affected: 5. Approximate students moved: 630. Number of goals met: 3. Pros: right sizes middle schools, resolves double splits, meets all three goals, keeps cohorts of students together. Cons: unresolved single splits, Hamilton splits from elementary to middle school, and Wattles, Smith and Baker have a split from middle to high school. Special education impact notes potential staffing increases at Smith, an opportunity for students with IEPs receiving services only or a resource room program to remain in a cohort with peers, potential for students placed in categorical programs to be displaced from peers if the placement is not at Smith, and continued staffing based on building need. English learner staffing continues based on need. Transportation routes and bus numbers may shift, with a goal of consistent routes and driver numbers and a longest route of 30 minutes or less.

**Option C - ONLY TU.** Baker 517, Boulan Park 793, Larson 625, Smith 591. Updated after the BOE Workshop on 1/14/25. All Troy Union students go to Smith; all students living in community housing go to Boulan Park Middle School (current policy); Somerset Apartments' 319 students go to Boulan Park from 6 elementary schools. Schools affected: 3. Approximate students moved: 250. Goals met: 2. Pro: resolves double splits. Cons: unresolved single splits, Hamilton splits from elementary to middle school, and Wattles, Smith and Baker have a middle-to-high school split. Special education and English learner staffing continue based on building need; transportation goals match Option C, with a longest route of 30 minutes or less.

**Option C - ONLY SA.** Baker 616, Boulan Park 603, Larson 750, Smith 557. Updated after the BOE Workshop on 1/14/25. Troy Union has no changes; all students living in community housing follow their currently assigned elementary school to that school's assigned middle school; Somerset Apartments' 319 students currently go to Boulan Park from 6 elementary schools. Schools affected: 3. Approximate students moved: 380. Goals met: 2. Pro: keeps cohorts of students together. Cons: does not resolve the Troy Union double split, unresolved single splits, Hamilton splits from elementary to middle school, and Wattles, Smith and Baker have a middle-to-high school split.

**Option C - TU to Larson.** Baker 616, Boulan Park 603, Larson 830, Smith 477. Updated after the BOE Workshop on 1/14/25. Troy Union all to Larson; all students living in community housing follow their currently assigned elementary school to that school's assigned middle school; Somerset Apartments' 319 students go to Boulan Park from 6 elementary schools. Schools affected: 6. Approximate students moved: 380. Goals met: 2. Pros: resolves double splits, keeps cohorts of students together. Cons: unresolved single splits, Hamilton splits from elementary to middle school, and Wattles, Smith and Baker have a middle-to-high school split.

**No Change.** All Somerset Apartment students go to Boulan Park. Four middle schools with 2,940 pupils (December 2024) and 2,526 pupils (2027). Existing Boundary (2024): Baker (Blue) 631, Boulan (Orange) 847, Larson (Green) 863, Smith (Yellow) 599. Maintain Existing Boundary/Policy (2027): Baker (Blue) 517, Boulan (Orange) 793, Larson (Green) 750, Smith (Yellow) 466. Schools affected: 0. Goals met: 1. Pros: no students affected, community support. Cons: does not right size middle schools, continues the disparity, maintains the double splits.

**Timeline and assumptions.** 2025/2026 - prepare for adjustments; 2026/2027 - changes implemented. Students will continue to have access to advanced programming. TSD will ensure families with multiple middle school students enrolled at the same time have the option to keep siblings at the same middle school. Middle school legacy: students currently enrolled in 5th, 6th, 7th or 8th grade (classes of 2032, 2031, 2030 and 2029) will not be impacted and may continue in the building they are in the Fall of 2025. Option to move: a current 5th or 6th grader slotted to attend a new school may do so in the 2025/2026 school year, ahead of the proposed changes. Curriculum is consistent across all four middle schools and athletics are uniform.

**Phases and next steps.** Phase 1 Discovery - committee formed, research and planning, potential recommendations developed. Phase 2 Recommendation (January) - the committee provides the Board with options and the Board determines whether to move forward. Phase 3 Feedback (February - April) - four listening sessions, one at each middle school, plus a community survey. Phase 4 Determination (April/May) - TSD provides the Board a summary of feedback and the Board determines any future changes. Next steps: February/March community meetings at the 4 middle schools; March/April community survey; April/May Board of Education consideration and decision.

2025_142_aarc_boe_presentation_final.paragraph: Delivered at the Troy School District Board of Education workshop on January 14, 2025, this Attendance Area Review Committee (AARC) presentation lays out the full slate of middle school boundary scenarios - Options A through E plus No Change - developed by a 25-member committee working with demographers Plante Moran. Options A, C, D and E are each shown as meeting all three goals, with the number of schools affected ranging from 4 under Option D to 9 under Options A and E. All scenarios are keyed to a projected Fall 2027 middle school enrollment of 2,526 students, down from 2,940 pupils in 2024.

**Document and setting.** Attendance Area Review Committee (AARC) Proposal presentation for the Troy School District, delivered to the Board of Education on January 14, 2025. It presents the committee's full option set - Options A, B, C, D and E plus a No Change scenario - for redrawing middle school attendance boundaries across the district's four middle schools: Baker, Boulan Park, Larson and Smith.

**Why the review.** Historic district practice is to review enrollment patterns and challenges every 5-10 years. Previous AARC groups met in 2015 and 2018. A 62-member Facilities Review Committee ran a 6-month process in 2021/22 to create recommendations for the 2022 bond proposal, with staff, student, cabinet and Board of Education feedback. District and community challenges include enrollment 'splits' as students transition from elementary to middle school or middle to high school, a double split at Troy Union, single splits at Smith, Baker, Wattles and Hamilton, world class programmatic experience, and current ratios at each middle school, where enrollment ranges from 590 to 870 per building. Additional factors are enrollment projections, birth rate and schools of choice, the new Smith Middle School built for an optimal enrollment of 750, and Metro Parent rankings placing all four middle schools in the Top 6 in Michigan.

**Optimal middle school size.** Ideal parameters are a Learning Community size of 125 students, average class size of 25 students, full-time teachers teaching 5 sections (5 x 25 = 125), two Learning Communities per grade level (250 in grade 6), and grades 6-8 totaling 750 students. Learning Communities can flex up to 900 students as class size increases above an average of 25, or to fewer than 750 students as class size dips below an average of 25, which increases costs. Benefits of optimal enrollment include elective staffing trending toward more full-time staff in the building and grade-level enrollment allowing 3 lunch periods aligned with grade levels.

A smaller school brings more partial staff, impact on school culture, limited availability of when courses are offered (example: only 2 sections of art offered), increased costs from lower class sizes, staff with split areas of focus across two content areas, and too few students for extracurricular courses such as jazz band, theatre and yearbook. A larger school may require staffing 'overages' (example: needing more than a 1.0 orchestra teacher), teachers giving up prep periods to teach overages, physical space congestion in classrooms, hallways and the cafeteria, saturated club and athletic opportunities, and limited ability to support new or move-in families due to high enrollment.

**Process to date.** The district hired Plante Moran as demographers for yearly and future enrollment projections. The AARC group was formed in 2024 with 25 members representing each elementary and middle school - 15 administrators and 10 community members - with applications requested in September from administrators, staff, families and cabinet. The 3-month process met on October 14, October 28, November 11, November 25 and December 9, and cabinet discussions have been held weekly since August 2024. Criteria and data utilized included enrollment, grade cohorts and boundaries, birth rates, resident/non-resident/employee feeder paths and patterns, current maps, demographic data covering ethnicity, English learners, students with disabilities, economics and content area performance, transportation implications, historical cohort data over time, and previous AARC information. Historical enrollment data slides carry a January 2024 label.

**Committee work.** TSD directed the committee to focus on a four middle school future and on how best to achieve a balanced distribution of enrollment. Committee feedback and further evaluation of data gave the district pause about how to better understand and uphold community priorities and values, with examples including programmatic experience, location and community schools, enrollment size in school, and duration of bus ride.

**Surrounding districts.** Rochester Community School District, Utica Community Schools, Walled Lake Consolidated Schools, Huron Valley Schools, West Bloomfield School District and Chippewa Valley Schools are noted as considering or moving through the same process.

**Goals.** Goal 1: right-size middle schools, equal student ratios. Goal 2: resolve double splits. Goal 3: no impact on high schools.

**Current pathways.** Troy Union to Smith/Larson to Athens/Troy; Wass, Hill and Costello to Larson to Athens; Barnard to Baker to Athens; Morse and Wattles to Baker to Athens/Troy; Martell and Leonard to Smith to Troy; Hamilton to Smith/Boulan to Troy; Schroeder and Bemis to Boulan to Troy. The double split is Troy Union Elementary students splitting between Smith and Larson middle schools, with the Smith students splitting again between Athens and Troy High. The elementary single split is Wattles and Morse Elementary students attending Baker MS being split between Troy HS and Athens HS. The middle school single split is Hamilton Elementary students splitting between Smith and Boulan Park MS, with both then attending Troy HS.

**Current and future student counts.** The four middle schools hold 2,940 pupils (2024) and a projected 2,526 pupils (2027). Existing Boundary (December 2024): Baker (Blue) 631 students, Boulan (Orange) 847 students, Larson (Green) 863 students, Smith (Yellow) 599 students. Maintain Existing Boundary (2027): Baker (Blue) 556, Boulan (Orange) 721, Larson (Green) 713, Smith (Yellow) 536.

**Fall 2027 projected middle school enrollment (2,526 students).** Hamilton 226, Schroeder 216, Bemis 237, Martell 189, Leonard 212, Wattles 205, Morse 204, Troy Union 205, Costello 219, Wass 219, Hill 187, Barnard 207. All options are based on the Fall 2027 projected enrollment.

**Option A.** Baker 631, Boulan Park 657, Larson 611, Smith 627. A portion of Morse and Wattles east of Rochester Rd. could split at the high school level. All of Hamilton goes to Smith, all of Morse goes to Boulan Park, all of Costello goes to Baker, and all of Troy Union goes to Larson. Number of schools affected: 9. Number of goals met: 3. Pros: right sizes middle schools, resolves a double split at Troy Union, middle school boundaries are geographically close to their middle school location, resolves all elementary-to-middle school splits, meets all three goals. Cons: Morse and Wattles maintain a middle-to-high school split, it affects the highest number of schools and students, it has two middle-to-high school splits at Baker and Boulan Park, and it impacts 4 elementary schools.

**Option B.** Baker 563, Boulan Park 739, Larson 611, Smith 613. Hamilton split, current, total 226: 150 to Boulan Park (2/3) and 76 to Smith (1/3). Cons: Morse, Wattles and Hamilton have an elementary-to-middle school split, several schools and students are affected, and a lot of disruption at the elementary level.

All students living in community housing follow their currently assigned elementary school to that elementary school's assigned middle school. Number of schools affected: 5. Number of goals met: 3. Pros: right sizes middle schools, resolves double splits, meets all three goals, keeps cohorts of students together. Cons: unresolved single splits, Hamilton splits from elementary to middle school, and Wattles, Smith and Baker have a middle-to-high school split.

**Option D.** Baker 616, Boulan Park 603, Larson 611, Smith 696. Hamilton split, current, total 226: 150 to Boulan Park (2/3) and 76 to Smith (1/3). All of Troy Union goes to Larson and all of Costello goes to Smith. Number of schools affected: 4. Number of goals met: 3. Pros: right sizes middle schools, resolves a double split at Troy Union, impacts fewer schools. Cons: Hamilton splits from elementary to middle school; Costello, Wattles and Morse split from middle to high school.

**Option E.** Baker 563, Boulan Park 589, Larson 611, Smith 763. Wattles split, current, total 205: 136 to Smith (2/3) and 69 to Baker (1/3). Morse split, total 204: 136 to Boulan Park (2/3) and 68 to Baker (1/3). All of Troy Union goes to Larson and all of Costello goes to Baker. Number of schools affected: 9. Number of goals met: 3. Pros: partially right sizes middle schools, resolves a double split at Troy Union, resolves all middle-to-high school splits, meets all three goals, and creates two distinct feeder patterns to Athens and Troy High with the split happening after elementary. Cons: Morse and Wattles have an elementary-to-middle school split, several schools and students are affected, and it impacts 9 buildings.

**No Change.** Current middle school boundary with four middle schools, 2,940 pupils (December 2024) and 2,526 pupils (2027). Existing Boundary (2024): Baker (Blue) 631, Boulan (Orange) 847, Larson (Green) 863, Smith (Yellow) 599. Maintain Existing Boundary (2027): Baker (Blue) 556, Boulan (Orange) 721, Larson (Green) 713, Smith (Yellow) 536. Number of schools affected: 0. Number of goals met: 1. Pros: no students affected, community support. Cons: does not right size middle schools, continues the disparity, maintains the double splits.

**Timeline and assumptions.** 2025/2026 - prepare for adjustments; 2026/2027 - changes implemented. Advanced programming: students will continue to have access. Siblings: TSD will ensure families with multiple middle school students enrolled at the same time have the option to keep siblings at the same middle school. Middle school legacy: students currently enrolled in 5th, 6th, 7th or 8th grade (classes of 2032, 2031, 2030 and 2029) will not be impacted and will have the option to continue in the building they are in the Fall of 2025. Option to move: a current 5th or 6th grader slotted to attend a new school may do so in the 2025/2026 school year, ahead of the proposed changes. Curriculum: the curriculum offered at all four middle schools is consistent across the district, and athletics are uniform.
